title: Diameter-one point set maximising far pairs
statement: For every natural number $n$, there exist points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ in the Euclidean plane $\bbr^2$ such that the set $\{x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n\}$ has diameter exactly $1$ and exactly $\lfloor n^2/3\rfloor$ of the unordered pairs $\{x_i, x_j\}$ satisfy $d(x_i, x_j) > 1/\sqrt{2}$, where $d$ denotes Euclidean distance.
hypotheses_covered: existence of n points in the Euclidean plane
the point set has diameter equal to 1
the number of pairs at distance greater than 1/sqrt(2) equals floor(n^2/3)
replaced:

\dots{}, x\_n\}} of diameter 1 with exactly \texttt{$\lfloor$n$^{2}$/3$\rfloor$} pairs
of points at distance greater than \texttt{1/$\sqrt{}$2}.}

Moreover, for each $n$, there is a set $\{x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n\}$ of diameter 1
with exactly $[n^2/3]$ pairs of points at distance greater than $1/\sqrt{2}$.
